audits.text:
## dff6bf5f78ab

**Reproduced defects — canonical legality rejection and false/inert control domains.** Audited generator SHA-256: `57f0d18bbbf112e84dc798e63bac054255794eb0fd76ffe164621453497c2a50`.

The strongest finding is that `self_check` rejects all four canonical inputs because it requires a one-cell distractor row that the canonical pairs do not contain. Exact pair shapes, row counts, and error messages are retained in `checks/audit/dff6bf5f78ab/reproduction.json`. The same probe shows that all three advertised degenerate textures (`no_pairs`, `single_singletons`, `three_in_row`) generate grids rejected by `self_check`.

The public control surface also accepts inert or undeclared values. `texture='default'`, `texture='warm'`, `palette_size=2`, `n_distinct_colors=2`, and `unknown_axis=123` were accepted and produced outputs byte-identical to the no-override control. The isolated defect lint failed with a blocking texture-domain-overlap issue, 135 strict-scalar warnings, four dead-texture warnings, structural mismatch, and no `RULE_HASH`; evidence is under `checks/audit/dff6bf5f78ab-defect-lint/`. No task-local tests were present (`checks/audit/dff6bf5f78ab-task-tests/result.json`, exit 5), so the executable reproduction at `checks/audit/dff6bf5f78ab/reproduce.py` is the focused coverage.

Recommended repair: make `self_check` describe legal authority inputs rather than a preferred teaching witness; move distractor requirements to semantic witness hooks; remove invalid degenerate textures from ordinary production; advertise only observable axes; reject unknown/inert keys and invalid scalars; add canonical acceptance and exact-override tests; declare the selected rule hash. These are reproduced contract defects. I did not edit the audited generator.
